\chapter{Review --- Three Places, One Question}
\label{ch:repaso-demostrativos}
\hlchaptermodality{225}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can choose the right pointing word without stopping to think.}

I can choose the right pointing word without stopping to think.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[(review)]{(review)}

\label{lesson:ES-C59-repaso-demostrativos}



\begin{quote}
Three words, three places, in order. (\emph{Este}, \emph{ese}, \emph{aquel}.)
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Three chants. Say each one, then say who it belongs to.

\textbf{First.} \emph{Este libro} — \textbf{by me}. The word Latin used to point at you, walked one step closer.

\textbf{Second.} \emph{Ese libro} — \textbf{by you}. The word that used to mean \emph{self}, moved in when the first one left.

\textbf{Third.} \emph{Aquel libro} — \textbf{by neither}. The word that also became \emph{el}, kept stressed and propped up so it could go on pointing.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: one question, asked twice}]
Everything else here is two questions, in this order.

\textbf{Do I have a noun?} If no, use the \emph{-o} form and stop: \emph{esto}, \emph{eso}, \emph{aquello}. Nothing to agree with, so nothing agrees.

\textbf{If yes — whose side is it on?} Then pick from the three, agree it with the noun, and put it \textbf{in front}, in the article's place. Never \emph{el este libro}; the pointing word already did the article's job.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item the three chants, in order, without looking
  \item \emph{¿Qué es esto?}, then answer it and point again with a noun
\end{itemize}

\emph{Twice through:}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Two origins worth keeping. What did \emph{ese} mean in Latin? (\emph{\textbf{Self}}.)

And which everyday word is \emph{aquel} related to? (\emph{\textbf{El}} — both from \emph{ille}, one worn down, one propped up.)
\end{tcolorbox}
